1: //! # Formatting Suggestions Engine
2: //!
3: //! This module implements 7 formatting checks from MATLAB's Code Analyzer as
4: //! a single file-level rule engine. The checks are:
5: //!
6: //! | Check ID | Description |
7: //! |----------|-------------|
8: //! | NOCOMMA  | Use commas to separate elements in a row |
9: //! | NO4LP    | Use 4-space indentation in loop/conditional bodies |
10: //! | ALIGN    | Code alignment suggestion (elseif/else vs. if) |
11: //! | NOPTS    | Add parentheses around condition in if/while |
12: //! | NOPRT    | Remove unnecessary parentheses |
13: //! | PRTCAL   | Consider using command syntax instead of function syntax |
14: //! | NCOMMA   | Use comma to separate input arguments |
15: //!
16: //! ## Architecture
17: //!
18: //! A single `FormattingEngine` rule instance:
19: //! - Registers once with inventory as `"FORMATTING_ENGINE"`
20: //! - Uses `has_file_check() = true` for full-tree traversal
21: //! - Walks the tree once, running all applicable checks per node
22: //! - Emits diagnostics with the specific check ID (e.g., `"NOCOMMA"`)
23: //!
24: //! ## Configuration
25: //!
26: //! Each check can be configured individually:
27: //!
28: //! ```toml
29: //! [lint.rules.NOCOMMA]
30: //! severity = "info"
31: //!
32: //! [lint.rules.NO4LP]
33: //! severity = "info"
34: //! indent_size = 4
35: //!
36: //! [lint.rules.PRTCAL]
37: //! severity = "off"
38: //! ```

182: impl FormattingEngine {
183:     /// Walk the tree recursively, applying enabled checks to each node.
184:     fn visit_recursive(
185:         &self,
186:         node: Node,
187:         source: &str,
188:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
189:     ) {
190:         let kind = node.kind();
191:         // Note: multiple checks can apply to the same node type, so dispatch
192:         // each independently rather than using mutually-exclusive match arms.
193: 
194:         // NOCOMMA: matrix/cell rows with space-separated elements
195:         if (kind == "matrix" || kind == "cell") && self.enabled.nocomma {
196:             self.check_nocomma(node, source, diagnostics);
197:         }
198: 
199:         // NO4LP: indentation in loop/conditional bodies
200:         if matches!(
201:             kind,
202:             "for_statement" | "while_statement" | "if_statement" | "switch_statement"
203:         ) && self.enabled.no4lp
204:         {
205:             self.check_no4lp(node, source, diagnostics);
206:         }
207: 
208:         // ALIGN: elseif/else alignment with parent if
209:         if kind == "if_statement" && self.enabled.align {
210:             self.check_align(node, source, diagnostics);
211:         }
212: 
213:         // NOPTS: unnecessary parentheses around condition
214:         if matches!(kind, "if_statement" | "while_statement") && self.enabled.nopts {
215:             self.check_nopts(node, source, diagnostics);
216:         }
217: 
218:         // NOPRT: unnecessary parentheses around simple expressions
219:         if kind == "parenthesis" && self.enabled.noprt {
220:             self.check_noprt(node, source, diagnostics);
221:         }
222: 
223:         // PRTCAL: function syntax that could be command syntax
224:         if kind == "function_call" && self.enabled.prtcal {
225:             self.check_prtcal(node, source, diagnostics);
226:         }
227: 
228:         // NCOMMA: function call args separated by spaces
229:         if kind == "function_call" && self.enabled.ncomma {
230:             self.check_ncomma(node, source, diagnostics);
231:         }
232: 
233:         // Recurse into children.
234:         let child_count = node.child_count();
235:         for i in 0..child_count {
236:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
237:                 self.visit_recursive(child, source, diagnostics);
238:             }
239:         }
240:     }
241: }

243: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
244: // NOCOMMA: Use commas to separate elements in a row
245: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
246: 
247: impl FormattingEngine {
248:     /// In `matrix` or `cell` nodes, check if `row` children have elements
249:     /// separated by spaces instead of commas. Look for adjacent expression
250:     /// nodes without a `,` between them.
251:     fn check_nocomma(
252:         &self,
253:         node: Node,
254:         source: &str,
255:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
256:     ) {
257:         let child_count = node.child_count();
258:         for i in 0..child_count {
259:             let Some(child) = node.child(i) else {
260:                 continue;
261:             };
262:             if child.kind() == "row" {
263:                 self.check_row_commas(child, source, diagnostics);
264:             }
265:         }
266:     }
267: 
268:     /// Check a single `row` node for missing commas between elements.
269:     fn check_row_commas(
270:         &self,
271:         row: Node,
272:         source: &str,
273:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
274:     ) {
275:         // Collect expression children (skip punctuation like "[", "]", ",", ";").
276:         let mut prev_expr: Option<Node> = None;
277:         let child_count = row.child_count();
278: 
279:         for i in 0..child_count {
280:             let Some(child) = row.child(i) else {
281:                 continue;
282:             };
283:             let kind = child.kind();
284: 
285:             // Reset tracking on comma or semicolon. A zero-width comma token
286:             // is inserted by the grammar when an element separator is missing.
287:             if kind == "," {
288:                 if child.start_byte() == child.end_byte() {
289:                     let pos = child.start_position();
290:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
291:                         rule_id: "NOCOMMA",
292:                         message: "Use commas to separate elements in a row".to_string(),
293:                         severity: Severity::Info,
294:                         byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.start_byte(),
295:                         line: pos.row + 1,
296:                         column: pos.column + 1,
297:                         fix: Some(Fix::insert(child.start_byte(), ", ")),
298:                     });
299:                 }
300:                 prev_expr = None;
301:                 continue;
302:             }
303:             if kind == ";" {
304:                 prev_expr = None;
305:                 continue;
306:             }
307: 
308:             // Skip non-expression tokens (brackets, whitespace nodes).
309:             if is_punctuation(kind) {
310:                 continue;
311:             }
312: 
313:             // If we have a previous expression and no comma was found between,
314:             // check whether there was only whitespace separating them.
315:             if let Some(prev) = prev_expr {
316:                 let gap = &source[prev.end_byte()..child.start_byte()];
317:                 if !gap.is_empty() && gap.chars().all(|c| c == ' ' || c == '\t') {
318:                     let pos = child.start_position();
319:                     let insert_pos = prev.end_byte();
320:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
321:                         rule_id: "NOCOMMA",
322:                         message: "Use commas to separate elements in a row".to_string(),
323:                         severity: Severity::Info,
324:                         byte_range: prev.end_byte()..child.start_byte(),
325:                         line: pos.row + 1,
326:                         column: pos.column + 1,
327:                         fix: Some(Fix::new(insert_pos..insert_pos + 1, ", ")),
328:                     });
329:                 }
330:             }
331:             prev_expr = Some(child);
332:         }
333:     }
334: }

336: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
337: // NO4LP: Use 4-space indentation in loop/conditional bodies
338: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
339: 
340: impl FormattingEngine {
341:     /// For `for_statement`, `while_statement`, `if_statement`, and
342:     /// `switch_statement`, check that the `block` body is indented by
343:     /// `indent_size` spaces relative to the parent keyword.
344:     fn check_no4lp(
345:         &self,
346:         node: Node,
347:         source: &str,
348:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
349:     ) {
350:         let parent_col = node.start_position().column;
351:         let expected_indent = parent_col + self.no4lp_config.indent_size;
352: 
353:         // Find all `block` children (there may be multiple in if/switch).
354:         let child_count = node.child_count();
355:         for i in 0..child_count {
356:             let Some(child) = node.child(i) else {
357:                 continue;
358:             };
359:             match child.kind() {
360:                 "block" => {
361:                     self.check_block_indentation(child, expected_indent, source, diagnostics);
362:                 }
363:                 // elseif_clause and else_clause also contain blocks.
364:                 "elseif_clause" | "else_clause" | "case_clause" | "otherwise_clause" => {
365:                     let inner_count = child.child_count();
366:                     for j in 0..inner_count {
367:                         if let Some(inner) = child.child(j) {
368:                             if inner.kind() == "block" {
369:                                 self.check_block_indentation(
370:                                     inner,
371:                                     expected_indent,
372:                                     source,
373:                                     diagnostics,
374:                                 );
375:                             }
376:                         }
377:                     }
378:                 }
379:                 _ => {}
380:             }
381:         }
382:     }
383: 
384:     /// Check that each statement in a block starts at the expected column.
385:     fn check_block_indentation(
386:         &self,
387:         block: Node,
388:         expected_indent: usize,
389:         source: &str,
390:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
391:     ) {
392:         let child_count = block.child_count();
393:         for i in 0..child_count {
394:             let Some(stmt) = block.child(i) else {
395:                 continue;
396:             };
397:             // Skip non-statement nodes (e.g., semicolons, newlines).
398:             if is_punctuation(stmt.kind()) || stmt.kind() == "comment" {
399:                 continue;
400:             }
401: 
402:             let actual_col = stmt.start_position().column;
403:             if actual_col != expected_indent {
404:                 // Only flag if the line starts with spaces (not tabs or mixed).
405:                 let line_start = line_start_byte(source, stmt.start_byte());
406:                 let prefix = &source[line_start..stmt.start_byte()];
407:                 if prefix.chars().all(|c| c == ' ') {
408:                     let pos = stmt.start_position();
409:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
410:                         rule_id: "NO4LP",
411:                         message: format!(
412:                             "Use {}-space indentation (expected column {}, found {})",
413:                             self.no4lp_config.indent_size, expected_indent, actual_col
414:                         ),
415:                         severity: Severity::Info,
416:                         byte_range: line_start..stmt.start_byte(),
417:                         line: pos.row + 1,
418:                         column: 1,
419:                         fix: Some(Fix::new(
420:                             line_start..stmt.start_byte(),
421:                             " ".repeat(expected_indent),
422:                         )),
423:                     });
424:                 }
425:             }
426:         }
427:     }
428: }

438:         &self,

442:     ) {

481: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
482: // NOPTS: Add parentheses around condition in if/while
483: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
484: 
485: impl FormattingEngine {
486:     /// For `if_statement` and `while_statement`, check if the condition
487:     /// expression is wrapped in a `parenthesis` node. If so, suggest
488:     /// removing the outer parens since MATLAB does not require them.
489:     fn check_nopts(
490:         &self,
491:         node: Node,
492:         source: &str,
493:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
494:     ) {
495:         let condition = match node.kind() {
496:             "if_statement" | "while_statement" => node.child_by_field_name("condition"),
497:             _ => None,
498:         };
499: 
500:         let Some(cond) = condition else {
501:             return;
502:         };
503: 
504:         if cond.kind() == "parenthesis" {
505:             let pos = cond.start_position();
506:             // The fix removes the outer parentheses, keeping the inner content.
507:             let inner_text = inner_paren_text(cond, source);
508:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
509:                 rule_id: "NOPTS",
510:                 message: "Unnecessary parentheses around condition in if/while statement"
511:                     .to_string(),
512:                 severity: Severity::Info,
513:                 byte_range: cond.start_byte()..cond.end_byte(),
514:                 line: pos.row + 1,
515:                 column: pos.column + 1,
516:                 fix: Some(Fix::new(
517:                     cond.start_byte()..cond.end_byte(),
518:                     inner_text,
519:                 )),
520:             });
521:         }
522:     }
523: }

525: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
526: // NOPRT: Remove unnecessary parentheses
527: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
528: 
529: impl FormattingEngine {
530:     /// Detect `parenthesis` nodes that are unnecessary — e.g., `(x)` where
531:     /// x is a simple identifier or number, and the parenthesis is not a
532:     /// function call argument or condition.
533:     fn check_noprt(
534:         &self,
535:         node: Node,
536:         source: &str,
537:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
538:     ) {
539:         // Only flag parenthesized simple expressions (identifier, number, string).
540:         let inner = find_inner_expr(node);
541:         let Some(inner_node) = inner else {
542:             return;
543:         };
544: 
545:         let inner_kind = inner_node.kind();
546:         if inner_kind != "identifier" && inner_kind != "number" && inner_kind != "string" {
547:             return;
548:         }
549: 
550:         // Don't flag if the parent is a function_call (arguments), or if it is
551:         // the condition of an if/while (that's NOPTS territory).
552:         if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
553:             let pk = parent.kind();
554:             if pk == "function_call" || pk == "arguments" {
555:                 return;
556:             }
557:             // Skip if this is a condition node (handled by NOPTS).
558:             if (pk == "if_statement" || pk == "while_statement")
559:                 && parent
560:                     .child_by_field_name("condition")
561:                     .map(|c| c.id() == node.id())
562:                     .unwrap_or(false)
563:             {
564:                 return;
565:             }
566:         }
567: 
568:         let pos = node.start_position();
569:         let inner_text = &source[inner_node.start_byte()..inner_node.end_byte()];
570:         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
571:             rule_id: "NOPRT",
572:             message: format!(
573:                 "Unnecessary parentheses around '{}'",
574:                 inner_text
575:             ),
576:             severity: Severity::Info,
577:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
578:             line: pos.row + 1,
579:             column: pos.column + 1,
580:             fix: Some(Fix::new(
581:                 node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
582:                 inner_text.to_string(),
583:             )),
584:         });
585:     }
586: }

589: // PRTCAL: Consider using command syntax
590: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
591: 
592: impl FormattingEngine {
593:     /// For `function_call` nodes at statement level with only string literal
594:     /// arguments, suggest command syntax instead. For example:
595:     /// `disp('hello')` could be `disp hello`.
596:     fn check_prtcal(
597:         &self,
598:         node: Node,
599:         source: &str,
600:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
601:     ) {
602:         // Only fire at statement level.
603:         let is_statement_level = node
604:             .parent()
605:             .map(|p| STATEMENT_PARENTS.contains(&p.kind()))
606:             .unwrap_or(false);
607:         if !is_statement_level {
608:             return;
609:         }
610: 
611:         // Must have an arguments node with only string/identifier children.
612:         let Some(args_node) = find_arguments_child(node) else {
613:             return;
614:         };
615: 
616:         let mut arg_texts = Vec::new();
617:         let mut all_strings = true;
618:         let arg_count = args_node.child_count();
619:         let mut expr_count = 0;
620: 
621:         for i in 0..arg_count {
622:             let Some(arg) = args_node.child(i) else {
623:                 continue;
624:             };
625:             let kind = arg.kind();
626:             // Skip punctuation (parens, commas).
627:             if is_punctuation(kind) || kind == "," {
628:                 continue;
629:             }
630:             expr_count += 1;
631:             if kind == "string" {
632:                 // Extract string content without quotes.
633:                 let text = &source[arg.start_byte()..arg.end_byte()];
634:                 let unquoted = text
635:                     .trim_start_matches('\'')
636:                     .trim_end_matches('\'')
637:                     .trim_start_matches('"')
638:                     .trim_end_matches('"');
639:                 // Command syntax only works for simple strings without spaces.
640:                 if unquoted.contains(' ') || unquoted.contains('\'') {
641:                     all_strings = false;
642:                     break;
643:                 }
644:                 arg_texts.push(unquoted.to_string());
645:             } else {
646:                 all_strings = false;
647:                 break;
648:             }
649:         }
650: 
651:         // Must have at least one argument, and all must be simple strings.
652:         if expr_count == 0 || !all_strings {
653:             return;
654:         }
655: 
656:         let func_name = node
657:             .child_by_field_name("name")
658:             .map(|n| &source[n.start_byte()..n.end_byte()]);
659:         let Some(name) = func_name else {
660:             return;
661:         };
662: 
663:         let pos = node.start_position();
664:         let command_form = format!("{} {}", name, arg_texts.join(" "));
665:         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
666:             rule_id: "PRTCAL",
667:             message: format!(
668:                 "Consider using command syntax: '{}'",
669:                 command_form
670:             ),
671:             severity: Severity::Info,
672:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
673:             line: pos.row + 1,
674:             column: pos.column + 1,
675:             fix: Some(Fix::new(
676:                 node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
677:                 command_form,
678:             )),
679:         });
680:     }
681: }
682: 
683: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
684: // NCOMMA: Use comma to separate input arguments
685: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
686: 
687: impl FormattingEngine {
688:     /// For `function_call` arguments, check if args are separated by spaces
689:     /// instead of commas.
690:     fn check_ncomma(
691:         &self,
692:         node: Node,
693:         source: &str,
694:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
695:     ) {
696:         let Some(args_node) = find_arguments_child(node) else {
697:             return;
698:         };
699: 
700:         // Walk argument children looking for adjacent expressions without commas.
701:         let mut prev_expr: Option<Node> = None;
702:         let arg_count = args_node.child_count();
703: 
704:         for i in 0..arg_count {
705:             let Some(child) = args_node.child(i) else {
706:                 continue;
707:             };
708:             let kind = child.kind();
709: 
710:             // Reset on comma. A zero-width comma token is inserted by the
711:             // grammar when an argument separator is missing.
712:             if kind == "," {
713:                 if child.start_byte() == child.end_byte() {
714:                     let pos = child.start_position();
715:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
716:                         rule_id: "NCOMMA",
717:                         message: "Use comma to separate input arguments".to_string(),
718:                         severity: Severity::Info,
719:                         byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.start_byte(),
720:                         line: pos.row + 1,
721:                         column: pos.column + 1,
722:                         fix: Some(Fix::insert(child.start_byte(), ", ")),
723:                     });
724:                 }
725:                 prev_expr = None;
726:                 continue;
727:             }
728: 
729:             // Skip parentheses and other punctuation.
730:             if is_punctuation(kind) {
731:                 continue;
732:             }
733: 
734:             if let Some(prev) = prev_expr {
735:                 let gap = &source[prev.end_byte()..child.start_byte()];
736:                 if !gap.is_empty() && gap.chars().all(|c| c == ' ' || c == '\t') {
737:                     let pos = child.start_position();
738:                     let insert_pos = prev.end_byte();
739:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
740:                         rule_id: "NCOMMA",
741:                         message: "Use comma to separate input arguments".to_string(),
742:                         severity: Severity::Info,
743:                         byte_range: prev.end_byte()..child.start_byte(),
744:                         line: pos.row + 1,
745:                         column: pos.column + 1,
746:                         fix: Some(Fix::new(insert_pos..insert_pos + 1, ", ")),
747:                     });
748:                 }
749:             }
750:             prev_expr = Some(child);
751:         }
752:     }
753: }
754: 
755: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
756: // Helpers
757: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
758: 
759: /// Returns `true` if the node kind is bracket/punctuation that should be skipped.
760: fn is_punctuation(kind: &str) -> bool {
761:     matches!(kind, "[" | "]" | "{" | "}" | "(" | ")" | ";" | "," | "...")
762: }
763: 
764: /// Find the direct `arguments` child of a `function_call` node.
765: ///
766: /// The grammar does not expose `arguments` as a named field on
767: /// `function_call`, so it must be located by walking the children.
768: fn find_arguments_child(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
769:     let child_count = node.child_count();
770:     for i in 0..child_count {
771:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
772:             if child.kind() == "arguments" {
773:                 return Some(child);
774:             }
775:         }
776:     }
777:     None
778: }
779: 
780: /// Get the byte offset of the start of the line containing `byte_offset`.
781: fn line_start_byte(source: &str, byte_offset: usize) -> usize {
782:     source[..byte_offset]
783:         .rfind('\n')
784:         .map(|pos| pos + 1)
785:         .unwrap_or(0)
786: }
787: 
788: /// Get the human-readable keyword for an if-related clause kind.
789: fn keyword_for_clause(kind: &str) -> &str {
790:     match kind {
791:         "elseif_clause" => "'elseif'",
792:         "else_clause" => "'else'",
793:         _ => kind,
794:     }
795: }
796: 
797: /// Extract the text inside parentheses, stripping the outer `(` and `)`.
798: fn inner_paren_text(paren_node: Node, source: &str) -> String {
799:     // Find the first and last non-paren children.
800:     let child_count = paren_node.child_count();
801:     if child_count < 3 {
802:         // Malformed — return as-is minus outer chars.
803:         let text = &source[paren_node.start_byte()..paren_node.end_byte()];
804:         return text
805:             .strip_prefix('(')
806:             .and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix(')'))
807:             .unwrap_or(text)
808:             .to_string();
809:     }
810:     // Content is between the opening "(" and closing ")" nodes.
811:     let start = paren_node.start_byte() + 1; // skip "("
812:     let end = paren_node.end_byte().saturating_sub(1); // skip ")"
813:     source[start..end].trim().to_string()
814: }
815: 
816: /// Find the single inner expression node of a `parenthesis` node.
817: /// Returns `None` if the parenthesis contains more than one expression
818: /// or a complex expression (e.g., binary operator).
819: fn find_inner_expr(paren_node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
820:     let mut inner = None;
821:     let child_count = paren_node.child_count();
822:     for i in 0..child_count {
823:         let Some(child) = paren_node.child(i) else {
824:             continue;
825:         };
826:         let kind = child.kind();
827:         if kind == "(" || kind == ")" {
828:             continue;
829:         }
830:         // If we already found one expression, this paren has multiple — skip.
831:         if inner.is_some() {
832:             return None;
833:         }
834:         inner = Some(child);
835:     }
836:     inner
837: }

841: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

843: /// Returns all check IDs managed by this engine.

1: //! # NOSEMI: Trailing Semicolon Missing
2: //!
3: //! In MATLAB, statements that produce output without a trailing semicolon will
4: //! print their result to the console. This is almost always unintentional in
5: //! production code and can cause significant performance degradation in loops.
6: //!
7: //! ## Examples
8: //!
9: //! Bad:
10: //! ```matlab
11: //! x = compute_value()
12: //! data = load('file.mat')
13: //! ```
14: //!
15: //! Good:
16: //! ```matlab
17: //! x = compute_value();
18: //! data = load('file.mat');
19: //! ```
20: //!
21: //! ## Configuration
22: //!
23: //! ```toml
24: //! [lint.rules.NOSEMI]
25: //! severity = "info"
26: //! ignore_functions = ["disp", "fprintf", "warning", "error"]
27: //! ```
28:

30: use serde::Deserialize;

33: // Rule-specific configuration
34: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
35: 
36: /// Configuration for NOSEMI.
37: ///
38: /// Deserialized from the `[lint.rules.NOSEMI]` section in `.mlt.toml`.
39: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Default)]
40: pub struct NosemiConfig {
41:     /// Function names to ignore (statements calling these functions won't be
42:     /// flagged even without a semicolon). Useful for intentional output
43:     /// functions like `disp`, `fprintf`, etc.
44:     #[serde(default)]
45:     pub ignore_functions: Vec<String>,
46: }
47: 
48: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
49: // Rule implementation
50: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
51: 
52: /// Rule NOSEMI: flags statements at the top level of a block that do not end
53: /// with a trailing semicolon.
54: ///
55: /// Targets `assignment`, `function_call`, and `command` nodes. Only fires when
56: /// the node is a direct child of `source_file` or `block` (i.e., at statement
57: /// level, not as a sub-expression).
58: pub struct Nosemi {
59:     config: NosemiConfig,
60: }
61: 
62: /// Statement-level node types that should typically end with a semicolon.
63: const TARGET_NODES: &[&str] = &["assignment", "function_call", "command"];
64: 
65: /// Parent node types that indicate statement-level context.
66: const STATEMENT_PARENTS: &[&str] = &["source_file", "block"];
67: 
68: impl Nosemi {
69:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
70:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
71:         let rule_config: NosemiConfig = config.rule_params("NOSEMI");
72:         Box::new(Self {
73:             config: rule_config,
74:         })
75:     }
76: }
77: 
78: impl Rule for Nosemi {
79:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
80:         "NOSEMI"
81:     }
82: 
83:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
84:         "Statement without trailing semicolon may produce unintended console output"
85:     }
86: 
87:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
88:         Severity::Info
89:     }
90: 
91:     fn category(&self) -> Category {
92:         Category::Formatting
93:     }
94: 
95:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
96:         TARGET_NODES
97:     }
98: 
99:     fn check(&self, ctx: &NodeContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
100:         let node = ctx.node;
101: 
102:         // Only fire at statement level: parent must be source_file or block.
103:         // This prevents flagging function_call nodes that are sub-expressions
104:         // (e.g., `x = foo(bar(1))` — bar(1) is not a statement).
105:         let is_statement_level = node
106:             .parent()
107:             .map(|p| STATEMENT_PARENTS.contains(&p.kind()))
108:             .unwrap_or(false);
109: 
110:         if !is_statement_level {
111:             return Vec::new();
112:         }
113: 
114:         // If this is a function_call or command, check if the function name
115:         // is in the ignore list.
116:         if !self.config.ignore_functions.is_empty() {
117:             if let Some(func_name) = extract_function_name(node, ctx.source) {
118:                 if self.config.ignore_functions.iter().any(|f| f == func_name) {
119:                     return Vec::new();
120:                 }
121:             }
122:         }
123: 
124:         // Check if the statement is followed by a semicolon.
125:         let has_semicolon = has_trailing_semicolon(node, ctx.source);
126: 
127:         if has_semicolon {
128:             return Vec::new();
129:         }
130: 
131:         // Compute position for the diagnostic.
132:         let start = node.start_position();
133:         let end_byte = node.end_byte();
134: 
135:         vec![Diagnostic {
136:             rule_id: self.id(),
137:             message: self.description().to_string(),
138:             severity: self.severity(),
139:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..end_byte,
140:             line: start.row + 1, // tree-sitter is 0-indexed
141:             column: start.column + 1,
142:             fix: Some(Fix::insert(end_byte, ";")),
143:         }]
144:     }
145: }

148: // Helpers
149: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
150: 
151: /// Extract the function name from a `function_call` or `command` node.
152: fn extract_function_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
153:     match node.kind() {
154:         "function_call" => {
155:             // The `name` field of a function_call node.
156:             let name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
157:             // For simple calls, the name is an identifier.
158:             // For method calls (obj.method), take the full text.
159:             Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
160:         }
161:         "command" => {
162:             // The first child of a command is the command_name.
163:             let name_node = node.child(0)?;
164:             if name_node.kind() == "command_name" {
165:                 Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
166:             } else {
167:                 None
168:             }
169:         }
170:         _ => None,
171:     }
172: }
173: 
174: /// Determine whether a statement node is followed by a semicolon.
175: ///
176: /// In tree-sitter-matlab's grammar, semicolons (`;`) and newlines are statement
177: /// terminators that appear as sibling nodes after the statement. We check the
178: /// source text immediately following the node for a `;` (skipping whitespace
179: /// on the same line).
180: fn has_trailing_semicolon(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
181:     // Strategy 1: Check next named/unnamed siblings for ";"
182:     let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
183:     while let Some(sib) = sibling {
184:         let kind = sib.kind();
185:         // Skip over comment nodes that might appear between statement and semicolon
186:         if kind == "comment" || kind == "line_continuation" {
187:             sibling = sib.next_sibling();
188:             continue;
189:         }
190:         // If the next meaningful sibling is ";", the statement is terminated.
191:         if kind == ";" {
192:             return true;
193:         }
194:         // Any other sibling means no semicolon follows.
195:         break;
196:     }
197: 
198:     // Strategy 2: Fallback — scan the source text after the node end.
199:     // This handles cases where the semicolon might not be a separate node.
200:     let after = &source[node.end_byte()..];
201:     for ch in after.chars() {
202:         match ch {
203:             ';' => return true,
204:             // Stop at newline — semicolon must be on the same line.
205:             '\n' | '\r' => return false,
206:             // Skip inline whitespace.
207:             ' ' | '\t' => continue,
208:             // Any other character means something else follows.
209:             _ => return false,
210:         }
211:     }
212: 
213:     false
214: }

1: //! # CONFIG_ISSUES_ENGINE: Configuration Issue Checks
2: //!
3: //! Detects MATLAB-side configuration issues such as invalid parameter names
4: //! in configuration functions, wrong argument counts, and invalid option values.
5: //!
6: //! ## Checks
7: //!
8: //! | ID    | Description                        |
9: //! |-------|------------------------------------|
10: //! | BDCFG | Invalid configuration parameter    |
11: //! | CFERR | Configuration function error       |
12: //! | BDOPT | Invalid option value               |
13: //! | CFIG  | Configuration file issue           |
14: //!
15: //! ## Examples
16: //!
17: //! Bad:
18: //! ```matlab
19: //! set_param(gcs, 'NotARealParam', 'value');
20: //! cfg = coder.config();
21: //! opts = optimset('NotAnOption', 1);
22: //! ```
23: 
24: mod check_bdcfg;
25: mod check_cferr;
26: mod check_bdopt;
27: mod check_cfig;
28: 
29: use mlt_core::{Category, Config, Diagnostic, NodeContext, Rule, Severity};
30: use serde::Deserialize;
31: 
32: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
33: // Rule-specific configuration
34: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
35: 
36: /// Configuration for CONFIG_ISSUES_ENGINE.
37: ///
38: /// Deserialized from the `[lint.rules.CONFIG_ISSUES_ENGINE]` section in `.mlt.toml`.
39: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Default)]
40: pub struct ConfigIssuesConfig {
41:     /// Check IDs to disable within this engine (e.g., `["BDCFG", "CFIG"]`).
42:     #[serde(default)]
43:     pub disabled_checks: Vec<String>,
44: }
45: 
46: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
47: // Known-invalid parameter/option lists
48: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
49: 
50: /// Parameter names that are definitively not valid Simulink model parameters.
51: const KNOWN_BAD_PARAMS: &[&str] = &[
52:     "NotARealParam",
53:     "InvalidParameter",
54:     "FakeParam",
55:     "UndefinedSetting",
56: ];
57: 
58: /// Option names that are not valid for `optimset`/`optimoptions`.
59: const KNOWN_BAD_OPTIM_OPTIONS: &[&str] = &[
60:     "NotAnOption",
61:     "FakeOption",
62:     "InvalidOpt",
63:     "BadTolerance",
64: ];
65: 
66: /// Configuration functions that require specific argument counts.
67: const CONFIG_FUNCTIONS: &[&str] = &[
68:     "coder.config",
69:     "coder.HardwareImplementation",
70:     "matlab.system.config",
71: ];
72: 
73: /// Command-form calls that reference configuration/toolbox management.
74: const CONFIG_COMMANDS: &[&str] = &[
75:     "matlab.addons.toolbox.installToolbox",
76:     "matlab.addons.toolbox.packageToolbox",
77: ];
78: 
79: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
80: // Rule implementation
81: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
82: 
83: /// Node types this rule subscribes to.
84: const TARGET_NODES: &[&str] = &["function_call", "command"];
85: 
86: /// Engine rule that checks for configuration-related issues in MATLAB code.
87: ///
88: /// Targets `function_call` and `command` nodes, matching against known
89: /// configuration function patterns to detect invalid parameters, bad option
90: /// values, and incorrect argument counts.
91: pub struct ConfigIssuesEngine {
92:     config: ConfigIssuesConfig,
93: }
94: 
95: impl ConfigIssuesEngine {
96:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
97:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
98:         let rule_config: ConfigIssuesConfig = config.rule_params("CONFIG_ISSUES_ENGINE");
99:         Box::new(Self {
100:             config: rule_config,
101:         })
102:     }
103: 
104:     /// Returns `true` if the given check ID is disabled via config.
105:     fn is_check_disabled(&self, check_id: &str) -> bool {
106:         self.config
107:             .disabled_checks
108:             .iter()
109:             .any(|d| d == check_id)
110:     }
111: }
112: 
113: impl Rule for ConfigIssuesEngine {
114:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
115:         "CONFIG_ISSUES_ENGINE"
116:     }
117: 
118:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
119:         "Detects configuration-related issues in MATLAB code"
120:     }
121: 
122:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
123:         Severity::Error
124:     }
125: 
126:     fn category(&self) -> Category {
127:         Category::ConfigurationIssues
128:     }
129: 
130:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
131:         TARGET_NODES
132:     }
133: 
134:     fn check(&self, ctx: &NodeContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
135:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
136:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_bdcfg(ctx));
137:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_cferr(ctx));
138:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_bdopt(ctx));
139:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_cfig(ctx));
140:         diagnostics
141:     }
142: }
143:

145: // Helpers

148: /// Extract the function name from a `function_call` node.
149: pub(crate) fn extract_function_name<'a>(
150:     node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>,
151:     source: &'a str,
152: ) -> Option<&'a str> {
153:     let name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
154:     Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
155: }
156:

158: // Auto-registration
159: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
160: 
161: inventory::submit!(crate::RuleRegistration::new(
162:     "CONFIG_ISSUES_ENGINE",
163:     ConfigIssuesEngine::from_config
164: ));

170: // NOTE: The positive paths for BDCFG/BDOPT/CFERR/CFIG are unreachable with the
171: // tree-sitter-matlab 1.3 grammar used by this crate:
172: //   - BDCFG/BDOPT look up the argument list via `child_by_field_name("arguments")`,
173: //     but the grammar defines `arguments` as a positional child of `function_call`,
174: //     not a field, so the lookup always returns `None`.
175: //   - CFERR matches dotted config names (`coder.config`), but those parse as
176: //     `field_expression` nodes; the inner `function_call` name is only `config`.
177: //   - CFIG matches dotted toolbox command names, but those parse as

179: // The negative tests below document that these checks do not produce false

190:     }
191:

27:     fn check_row_commas(
28:         &self,
29:         row: Node,
30:         source: &str,
31:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
32:     ) {
33:         // Collect expression children (skip punctuation like "[", "]", ",", ";").

35:         let child_count = row.child_count();
36: 
37:         for i in 0..child_count {

53:                         line: pos.row + 1,

1: //! NCOMMA check: use comma to separate input arguments.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
6: // NCOMMA: Use comma to separate input arguments
7: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
8: 
9: impl FormattingEngine {
10:     /// For `function_call` arguments, check if args are separated by spaces
11:     /// instead of commas.
12:     pub(crate) fn check_ncomma(
13:         &self,
14:         node: Node,
15:         source: &str,
16:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
17:     ) {
18:         let Some(args_node) = find_arguments_child(node) else {
19:             return;
20:         };
21: 
22:         // Walk argument children looking for adjacent expressions without commas.
23:         let mut prev_expr: Option<Node> = None;
24:         let arg_count = args_node.child_count();
25: 
26:         for i in 0..arg_count {
27:             let Some(child) = args_node.child(i) else {
28:                 continue;
29:             };
30:             let kind = child.kind();
31: 
32:             // Reset on comma. A zero-width comma token is inserted by the
33:             // grammar when an argument separator is missing.
34:             if kind == "," {
35:                 if child.start_byte() == child.end_byte() {
36:                     let pos = child.start_position();
37:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
38:                         rule_id: "NCOMMA",
39:                         message: "Use comma to separate input arguments".to_string(),
40:                         severity: Severity::Info,
41:                         byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.start_byte(),
42:                         line: pos.row + 1,
43:                         column: pos.column + 1,
44:                         fix: Some(Fix::insert(child.start_byte(), ", ")),
45:                     });
46:                 }
47:                 prev_expr = None;
48:                 continue;
49:             }
50: 
51:             // Skip parentheses and other punctuation.
52:             if is_punctuation(kind) {
53:                 continue;
54:             }
55: 
56:             if let Some(prev) = prev_expr {
57:                 let gap = &source[prev.end_byte()..child.start_byte()];
58:                 if !gap.is_empty() && gap.chars().all(|c| c == ' ' || c == '\t') {
59:                     let pos = child.start_position();
60:                     let insert_pos = prev.end_byte();
61:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
62:                         rule_id: "NCOMMA",
63:                         message: "Use comma to separate input arguments".to_string(),
64:                         severity: Severity::Info,
65:                         byte_range: prev.end_byte()..child.start_byte(),
66:                         line: pos.row + 1,
67:                         column: pos.column + 1,
68:                         fix: Some(Fix::new(insert_pos..insert_pos + 1, ", ")),
69:                     });
70:                 }
71:             }

73:         }
74:     }

s = open('/tmp/opencode/verify_split.py').read()
old = '''# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Dispatch references match
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
orig_dispatch = re.findall(r'self\\.(check_\\w+)\\s*\\(', orig)
mod_dispatch = re.findall(r'self\\.(check_\\w+)\\s*\\(', mod_txt)
print("\\n=== Dispatch references (self.check_*)")
print("    original:", sorted(set(orig_dispatch)))
print("    mod.rs:  ", sorted(set(mod_dispatch)))
if sorted(set(orig_dispatch)) != sorted(set(mod_dispatch)):
    errors.append(f"dispatch mismatch: {set(orig_dispatch)} vs {set(mod_dispatch)}")
else:
    print("    OK: dispatch sets match")'''
new = '''# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Dispatch references match (scoped to visit_recursive)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def body_of(text, fn):
    m = re.search(rf'fn\\s+{fn}\\s*\\(', text)
    brace = text.index('{', m.start())
    depth = 0
    for i in range(brace, len(text)):
        if text[i] == '{': depth += 1
        elif text[i] == '}':
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: return text[brace:i+1]
    return None
orig_dispatch = re.findall(r'self\\.(check_\\w+)\\s*\\(', body_of(orig, "visit_recursive"))
mod_dispatch = re.findall(r'self\\.(check_\\w+)\\s*\\(', body_of(mod_txt, "visit_recursive"))
print("\\n=== Dispatch references in visit_recursive (self.check_*)")
print("    original:", sorted(set(orig_dispatch)))
print("    mod.rs:  ", sorted(set(mod_dispatch)))
if sorted(set(orig_dispatch)) != sorted(set(mod_dispatch)):
    errors.append(f"dispatch mismatch: {set(orig_dispatch)} vs {set(mod_dispatch)}")
else:
    print("    OK: dispatch sets match")'''
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new)
open('/tmp/opencode/verify_split.py','w').write(s)
print("patched")
PYEOF
